notes: ICS runs its own after-school program at the school, the 21st Century Community Learning Center, funded by the Pennsylvania Department of Education. It has a listing here; ask the school how to sign up and whether it costs anything.

ICS keeps its own calendar, and its days off aren’t the District’s: it is open on Veterans Day and on November 16, for instance, and closed on December 11 and March 19 for report card days. The days off on this page come from the ICS calendar; the days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against ICS’s.

Wednesdays are early-dismissal days at ICS, and programs handle them differently. ICS’s own program starts at 1:30 pm that day, Philly InMovement picks up from ICS on Wednesdays only, ZAZZ charges extra for its Wednesday early pickup, and Beehive doesn’t pick up on ICS’s half-day Wednesdays. Ask each program how Wednesdays work.
If you know a program that serves ICS and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

If you know a program that serves Cook-Wissahickon and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

If you know a program that serves C.W. Henry and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

notes: Thomas Elementary’s own page says it offers aftercare through two providers, Mastermindz and SafeHaven, from dismissal to 6:00 pm, Monday to Friday. Neither provider has a website we could find, so both listings rest on the school’s page; the school’s page gives a contact number for each.

Thomas follows the Mastery Schools calendar, not the District’s. Its days off on this page come from Mastery’s 2026–27 Philadelphia calendar: it closes for Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, and its spring break is March 22 to 26. Mastery’s calendar marks early dismissals on November 10, December 23, February 9, May 7 and June 11 (the last day). Ask each aftercare provider whether it covers those afternoons.
Thomas Elementary teaches kindergarten to 6th grade; its students can go on to the Mastery Thomas Campus for 7th to 12th grade, which is a separate building at 927 Johnston St.
If you know a program that serves Mastery Thomas and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Juniata Park Academy
address: 801 E Hunting Park Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19124
dismissalNote: kindergarten to 2nd grade at 2:45 pm, 3rd and 4th at 2:50 pm, and 5th to 8th at 2:54 pm; on half days 11:50 am (11:54 am for 5th to 8th)
notes: Juniata Park’s own site says its after-school program is run by the YMCA. The City lists the YMCA’s free before care (7:00 to 8:30 am) and after school (2:45 to 6:00 pm) at the school for kindergarten to 8th grade.
After-School All-Stars runs a free program at the school on Tuesdays and Thursdays for 5th to 8th graders.
The school’s site also lists clubs (STEAM, robotics, art, Girls on the Run and others) without days or times. Ask the office which run after school.
If you know a program that serves Juniata Park and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Joseph Greenberg School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule, last updated in 2021, shows homeroom at 7:30 am and dismissal at 2:05 to 2:09 pm
notes: Two free after-school programs run in the building, both part of the City’s Extended Day program: the Boys & Girls Club at Greenberg, which the Boys & Girls Clubs of Philadelphia list as a school extension site for enrolled students, and the Philly KiDZ Initiative. Greenberg’s own site doesn’t describe either one.
Greenberg’s bell schedule page was last updated in 2021. Ask the office for this year’s dismissal time, and ask each program what it does on half days.
If you know a program that serves Greenberg and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: D. Newlin Fell School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives a school day of 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, with breakfast from 8:30 am
notes: Greater Philadelphia Community Alliance (GPCA) runs Fell’s after-school program: GPCA’s own page lists Fell among the schools it serves, and Fell names GPCA as a community partner. Girls on the Run also has a team at Fell this fall.
Fell’s page lists clubs, among them art, chess, choir, reading, Scrabble and intramural sports, without saying whether they meet after school. Ask the office which ones run after dismissal.
Fell’s site points to its parent and student handbook for early dismissals. Ask GPCA what it does on half days.
If you know a program that serves Fell and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Fell
alsoListed.intro: Fell’s own site names these, but we couldn’t confirm them on the program’s own page this time.
items: ASAP Philly (After-school Activities Program): on Fell’s list of community partners. ASAP’s site turned away our reader, so we couldn’t check which schools it serves. phillyasap.org

name: Alain Locke School
dismissalNote: the school’s site says school starts at 8:45 am and doesn’t post a dismissal time
notes: Community Council’s ACE (Artistic & Cultural Enrichment) after-school program runs at Locke, free, 3:00 to 6:00 pm on weekdays, according to the City’s program locator. Girls on the Run also has a team at Locke this fall.
Locke’s own site is thin: it gives the start of the school day but no dismissal time, after-school page or partners list. Ask the office for the dismissal time and what happens on half days.

Lee Cultural Center, a City rec center about a fifth of a mile east on Haverford Avenue, lists an after-school program for ages 6 to 12. Its listing doesn’t mention picking children up from the school.
If you know a program that serves Locke and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Richmond School
dismissalNote: the school’s daily schedule gives a school day of 9:00 am to 3:39 pm; before-school clubs may start at 7:45 am, first come, first served, and it says after-school programs end at 4:45 pm
notes: Early Life Academy runs free after care at Richmond: its own page lists the school, and the City’s program locator gives 3:30 to 6:00 pm on weekdays. Richmond’s schedule page says after-school programs end at 4:45 pm, so ask Early Life Academy which time applies. Girls on the Run also has a team at Richmond this fall.
Richmond’s schedule page has a separate half-day lunch schedule. Ask Early Life Academy whether it opens early on half days.
Cohocksink Recreation Center, a City rec center about a fifth of a mile away, lists an after-school program for ages 6 to 13. Its listing doesn’t mention picking children up from the school.
If you know a program that serves Richmond and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Stephen Girard School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives a school day of 8:15 am to 2:45 pm, with breakfast from 7:45 am
notes: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Philadelphia list Stephen Girard as one of their school extension sites, and Girard names the club among its community partners; neither posts the site’s hours. Girls on the Run also has a team at Girard this fall.
Girard’s page lists clubs (Cub Scouts, robotics, math, garden, art, STEM) and intramural sports without saying when they meet. Ask the office which ones run after school.

Two places within about half a mile run after-school programs, though neither says it picks up from Girard: Caring People Alliance’s South Philadelphia Boys & Girls Club on South 15th Street, and DiSilvestro Playground at 15th and Morris.
If you know a program that serves Stephen Girard and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Stephen Girard
alsoListed.intro: Girard’s site lists these among its community partners, but we couldn’t confirm an after-school program at the school on the program’s own page or the City’s locator this time.
items: Al-Bustan Seeds of Culture: Arab arts classes. The City’s locator lists Al-Bustan’s after-school program at another school this year, not Girard. albustanseeds.org
Young Chances Foundation: a Grays Ferry youth organization. Its site doesn’t mention Girard. youngchances.org
Rock Reach and Dance Exchange / BalletX: named as partners, with no details on Girard’s site.

name: Thomas Mifflin School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives a school day of 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, with breakfast at 8:45 am
notes: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Philadelphia list Mifflin as one of their school extension sites, and Mifflin names the Wissahickon Boys and Girls Club among its partners; neither posts the site’s hours. Girls on the Run also has a team at Mifflin this fall.
Mifflin’s page lists clubs, among them anime, chess, debate, LEGO STEM, Scrabble and a spring musical, without saying when they meet. Ask the office which ones run after school.
No City rec center after-school program is listed within a mile of Mifflin.
If you know a program that serves Mifflin and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Mifflin
alsoListed.intro: Mifflin’s own site names these, but we couldn’t confirm them on the program’s own page this time.
items: Philadelphia Youth Basketball: on Mifflin’s list of clubs and activities. PYB’s own site doesn’t name the school; its Sixth Man Center is on Wissahickon Avenue, about a mile away. phillyyouthbasketball.org

name: Paul L. Dunbar School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives a school day of 7:30 am to 2:09 pm, with breakfast in the classroom from 7:30
notes: Dunbar’s own site says it is a Community School with many after-school programs, without naming them, and asks families to contact the main office about them.
The Greater Philadelphia YMCA lists Dunbar as one of its free after-school sites, and Girls on the Run has a team at Dunbar this fall.
For early dismissals and half days, Dunbar’s site points to the Parent & Student Handbook. Ask the office whether the YMCA program runs on those days.
If you know a program that serves Dunbar and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Cayuga School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:15 am to 2:54 pm, according to the school’s site, which also posts a dismissal procedure for 3rd to 5th graders
notes: Cayuga’s own site doesn’t name an after-school program. The City’s program locator lists Catholic Charities’ free after-school program at the school, and Girls on the Run has a team at Cayuga this fall.
Cayuga’s site doesn’t say what happens on half days. Ask the office, and ask Catholic Charities whether its program runs on those afternoons.
If you know a program that serves Cayuga and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Bayard Taylor School
dismissalNote: the school day is 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, with breakfast for grades 1–5 from 8:30, according to the school’s bell schedule
notes: Bayard Taylor’s own site names the Boys and Girls Club and Girls on the Run among its community partners, and the Boys & Girls Clubs list the school as one of their school extension sites, open to children enrolled at the school.

The site also lists clubs and activities without saying when they meet: art, dance, gardening, jump rope, music, Kensington Soccer and Dance Educators of America among them. Ask the office which ones run after school.
For early dismissals and half days, the site points to the Parent & Student Handbook. Ask the office what the after-school programs do on those days.
If you know a program that serves Bayard Taylor and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Bayard Taylor
alsoListed.intro: Bayard Taylor’s own site names these, but we couldn’t confirm an after-school program for the school on the program’s own page or in the City’s listings this time.
items: Taller Puertorriqueño: the school lists a Taller Visitenos art program under arts, music and dance, without saying whether it meets after school. tallerpr.org
Girls Inc. of Philadelphia: on the school’s list of community partners. The City’s locator lists Girls Inc. programs elsewhere, not at Bayard Taylor. girlsincphillysnj.org

Legacy Youth Tennis and Education: the City’s locator lists a free Legacy after-school program “at McClure” at 3698 N Randolph St, which is Bayard Taylor’s address. McClure is a different school, on W Hunting Park Ave, so ask Legacy which school the program serves. legacyyte.org

name: John Moffet School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:15 am to 2:54 pm, according to the school’s bell schedule; the building opens at 8:00 for breakfast
notes: Moffet’s own extracurriculars page lists Girls on the Run, Al-Bustan’s drumming lessons, STEM clubs, a sports club and a book club after school. Only Girls on the Run and the drumming have listings here; the page doesn’t give days for the clubs, so ask the office.
Xiente (formerly Norris Square Community Alliance) lists Moffet as one of its Out of School Time sites, and the City’s program locator lists its free after care at the school.
Moffet’s site doesn’t say what happens on half days. Ask the office, and ask Xiente whether its program runs on those afternoons.
If you know a program that serves Moffet and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Anne Frank School
dismissalNote: the school day is 7:30 am to 2:09 pm; kindergarten is dismissed at 1:55 pm. On half days kindergarten leaves at 10:55 am and grades 1–5 at 11:09 am
notes: Anne Frank’s own site says its after-school programming is provided by Philly KiDZ, Monday to Friday, 2:09 to 6:00 pm, with academic support and enrichment, and the City’s program locator lists the same program at the school.
The site lists Girls on the Run and clubs (chess, LEGO robotics, art, drawing, running, games and others) without saying when they meet. Ask the office which ones run after school.
On half days the school lets out at 11:09 am (10:55 am for kindergarten). Ask Philly KiDZ whether it opens early on those days.
If you know a program that serves Anne Frank and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: William D. Kelley School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:15 am to 2:54 pm
notes: Kelley’s own site lists a YMCA Afterschool Program among its activities, and the Greater Philadelphia YMCA lists Kelley among the schools where it runs its free, City-funded after-school program, to 5:30 pm. It has a listing here.

The school’s site also lists clubs and activities (Art Club, WHYY Media Club, Girls Inc., a male mentoring program, tutoring and a fitness club) without days, times or grades. Ask the office which are running this year.
Kelley’s site points to its Parent & Student Handbook for early dismissals. Ask the YMCA what happens on half days before counting on one.
If you know a program that serves Kelley and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Penn Alexander School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:30 am to 3:09 pm
notes: The School District’s list calls the school Sadie Alexander School; its own site calls it Penn Alexander School.

Parent Infant Center’s After School Center, on the same block of Spruce Street, says its teachers meet children at Penn Alexander and walk them over, for kindergarten to 4th grade. It also offers full days on District holidays.

Penn Alexander’s own clubs run in fall, winter and spring cycles depending on student interest and teacher availability; the school’s site lists them without days or times. Ask the office which are running this season.

The City’s program locator lists no after-school program inside Penn Alexander. The nearest is the University of Pennsylvania’s program inside Lea, about half a mile west; ask there whether it takes children from other schools.
If you know a program that serves Penn Alexander and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Penn Alexander
alsoListed.intro: Penn Alexander’s own site names this among its community partners, and we haven’t confirmed what it runs at the school.
items: ASAP, listed by the school among its community partners. ASAP’s own site couldn’t be reached today, so we don’t know what it runs at Penn Alexander.

name: Edward Gideon School
dismissalNote: the school day is 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, and half days end at 12:39 pm
notes: The Greater Philadelphia YMCA lists Gideon among the schools where it runs its free, City-funded after-school program, to 5:30 pm, and Gideon names the YMCA among its partners. The City’s program data also has a YMCA morning program at Gideon from 7:00 am. Both are in one listing here.

Gideon’s site lists brass and string lessons, a drumline, a dance ensemble, Philadelphia Youth Basketball, Girls Inc.’s HYPE, Mural Arts, and gardening and cooking clubs, without days, times or grades. Ask the office which are running this year.

Gideon also names Methodist Services among its partners. Methodist Services’ own page says it provides case management for families at Gideon as part of the City’s Community Schools program, not an after-school program.
Gideon’s half days end at 12:39 pm. Ask the YMCA whether it opens early on those days.
If you know a program that serves Gideon and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: James G. Blaine School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:15 am to 2:54 pm
notes: Blaine’s own site lists the YMCA among its extracurricular programs and says sign-up is posted on Class Dojo. The YMCA lists Blaine among the schools where it runs its free, City-funded after-school program, and the City’s locator lists it too. It has a listing here.

Blaine also lists the Philadelphia Arts in Education Partnership, optional weekly strings lessons, and fall, winter and spring teams for 6th to 8th graders, without days or times. Ask the office what is running this year.
Blaine’s site names the Honickman center among its programs too. It is a few blocks away on Judson Street, and the City’s locator lists Project HOME’s program there for teens.
Blaine’s site points to its Parent & Student Handbook for early dismissals. Ask the YMCA what happens on half days.
If you know a program that serves Blaine and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Francis Hopkinson School
dismissalNote: the school’s site doesn’t post a bell schedule; it says doors open at 8:55 am
notes: The Greater Philadelphia YMCA lists Hopkinson among the schools where it runs its free, City-funded after-school program, to 5:30 pm. Hopkinson’s own site doesn’t mention it. It has a listing here.
Hopkinson’s extracurriculars page lists a book club, coding, dance, STEM, Math24, yoga, running and school teams, without days, times or grades. Ask the office which are running this year.
Hopkinson’s site doesn’t post a bell schedule or half-day times. Ask the office when the school day ends, and ask the YMCA what happens on half days.
If you know a program that serves Hopkinson and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Edward T. Steel School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives dismissal as 3:30 to 3:39 pm, and 12:30 to 12:40 pm on half days
notes: GPCA (Greater Philadelphia Community Alliance) runs a free after-school program in the building for Steel students, and a free before-care from 7:30 am, according to the City’s program locator. It has a listing here.

Steel’s own site lists after-school clubs run by its staff, from homework clubs to a step team, and says to visit the main office to find out how to join. That page was last updated in January 2025, so ask which clubs are running this year.
On half days Steel dismisses at 12:30 pm. The City’s listing for GPCA doesn’t say whether the program runs on half days, so ask GPCA.
If you know a program that serves Steel and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Ad Prima Charter School, Mt. Airy Campus
aliases: Ad Prima Charter School Mt. Airy Campus
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, later than most schools; its calendar shows 12:00 pm dismissal on early-dismissal days

days.name: Winter recess and New Year’s Day
Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day

notes: Ad Prima says it has no before- or after-school care: its school day runs to 4:00 pm. Its clubs meet after that, 4:00 to 5:30 pm, on the days its monthly calendar shows. In November 2026 that was chess and Girls on the Run on Mondays, robotics, spirit team and orators on Tuesdays, and theater, robotics and Girls on the Run on Thursdays. They have listings here.

Ad Prima keeps its own calendar, and its days off aren’t the District’s: it is closed for Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr and Good Friday, for instance, and dismisses early for report card conferences (November 16–18, February 4–5 and April 15–16). The days off on this page come from Ad Prima’s calendar; the days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against Ad Prima’s.
This page is for the Mt. Airy campus. Ad Prima’s other campus is in Overbrook, at 1922 N 63rd St.
If you know a program that serves Ad Prima and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Russell H. Conwell School
aliases: Russell H. Conwell Middle Magnet School
dismissalNote: the school’s hours page, last updated in 2022, gives the school day as 7:30 am to 2:30 pm; ask the office for this year’s times
notes: Conwell is a middle school, 5th to 8th grade. The Philadelphia Youth Network runs a free after-school program in the building for Conwell students: PYN lists Conwell among its 2026–27 sites, and the school’s flyer for 2025–26 gave Monday to Friday, 2:34 to 5:45 pm. Philadelphia Ballet’s free Let’s Dance program is at Conwell this year too, according to the school’s flyer. Both have listings here, as do the activities Conwell names on its own site.
Conwell’s site doesn’t post a half-day schedule. Ask the office, and ask PYN whether its program runs on half days.
If you know a program that serves Conwell and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Middle Years Alternative School
aliases: Middle Years Alternative School for the Humanities
Middle Years Academy for Innovation and Career Exploration
dismissalNote: the school’s site posts no bell schedule; it says students won’t be released early after 2:15 pm, so ask the office for the dismissal time
notes: MYA is a middle school, 5th to 8th grade, with citywide admission. Episcopal Community Services runs a free after-school program in the building, 3:00 to 6:00 pm on weekdays, according to the City’s program locator, and MYA’s own site names ECS’s out-of-school programming. It has a listing here, as do MYA’s sports teams and music groups.
MYA’s site doesn’t post a half-day schedule. Ask the office, and ask ECS whether its program runs on half days.
If you know a program that serves MYA and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also on MYA’s own site
alsoListed.intro: MYA’s “Points of Pride” page, last updated in May 2024, names these too. We couldn’t confirm them for this year.
items: An after-school cooking club with the Agatston Urban Nutrition Initiative at Penn’s Netter Center. The Netter Center’s page doesn’t name MYA. nettercenter.upenn.edu

Boxing club and chess, which the page lists as part of Episcopal Community Services’ out-of-school programming. The City’s 2026–27 listing for ECS at MYA names cooking, basketball and field trips instead.

name: Martha Washington School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives the school day as 9:00 am to 3:39 pm
notes: Community Council’s ACE (Artistic & Cultural Enrichment) program runs after school in the building, free, Monday to Friday until 6:00 pm, according to the City’s program locator, and Martha Washington’s own site names it too. It has a listing here.

The school’s after-school page also lists an after-school dance group on Mondays and Wednesdays, 4:00 to 5:30 pm. That page was last updated in February 2024, so ask the office whether it meets this year.
Martha Washington’s site doesn’t post a half-day schedule. Ask the office, and ask Community Council whether ACE runs on half days.
If you know a program that serves Martha Washington and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Alexander Adaire School
dismissalNote: the school’s site gives the bell schedule as 8:30 am to 3:09 pm
notes: Adaire’s own family handbook (the 2025–26 edition, linked from its site; the 2026–27 one is marked “coming soon”) names four programs that provide after-school care and pick up at Adaire: PlayArts, which runs inside the school, Fishtown Rec Center and Shissler Rec Center, which walk children over, and STEM Prep Academy. Each has a listing here.

The handbook also says clubs meet after school for 60 to 90 minutes on different days through the year (drama, Catapult STEM for 3rd and 4th grade, journalism, flag football, basketball, and a STEAM program for 5th to 8th grade), and that these are not full-time care. Which ones run changes during the year, so ask your child’s teacher.

PlayArts says the School Board dropped the scheduled half days from the 2026–27 District calendar, so its program at Adaire runs from dismissal every school day; when the District is closed, its full-day camps are at the Maas Building. Ask the rec centers and STEM Prep what they do on days off.
If you know a program that serves Adaire and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named in Adaire’s handbook
alsoListed.intro: Adaire’s 2025–26 handbook lists this among its after-school activities. We couldn’t confirm it for this year.
items: Girls on the Run. Its own Fall 2026 list of team sites doesn’t include Adaire, so ask the school whether there is a team this spring.

name: Community Academy of Philadelphia Charter School
dismissalNote: the school’s calendar gives the elementary school’s day (kindergarten to 8th grade) as 8:00 am to 3:00 pm, and 8:00 am to 1:00 pm on “B schedule” days
notes: Community Academy’s own club guides for 2026–27 list after-school clubs run by its teachers on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, from September to December and again from January to May. Clubs end at 3:45 pm sharp, and children must be picked up then. Places are limited and go first come, first served: email the teacher the guide names for a permission slip. They have a listing here.
Girls on the Run lists a team here in its Fall 2026 sites, and the school’s 5th–8th grade guide lists its Heart & Sole team for grades 6 to 8.
We found no daily after-school care on Community Academy’s site. Ask the office whether there is any, and who runs it.

Community Academy keeps its own calendar, and its days off aren’t the District’s: it is closed September 4–7, October 23, March 19 (Founder’s Day), March 24–29 for spring break, April 23 and May 28–31, for instance, and ends at 1:00 pm on “B schedule” days. The days off on this page come from its calendar; the days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against the school’s.
Community Academy teaches kindergarten to 12th grade at 1100 E Erie Ave. Kindergarten and 8th grade finish on June 10, the rest of the elementary school on June 11.
If you know a program that serves Community Academy and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Mastery Prep Elementary
dismissalNote: the school’s page gives the school day as 7:45 am to 3:35 pm
notes: Mastery Prep’s own page names two after-school care options: Change 4 A Dollar, which offers before- and after-school care, from dismissal to 6:00 pm, Monday to Friday, open to all students, and a Boys & Girls Club, which offers after-school care only. It says sign-up details come to families through ParentSquare. Change 4 A Dollar has a listing here; the page doesn’t say which Boys & Girls Club, so it is listed with the school’s clubs; ask the school which club it means and how children get there.
The page also lists the school’s own clubs and teams: boys’ and girls’ basketball, dance, homework club, drumline and art club. They have a listing here.

Mastery Prep follows the Mastery Schools calendar, not the District’s. Its days off on this page come from Mastery’s 2026–27 Philadelphia calendar: it closes for Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, and its spring break is March 22 to 26. The days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against Mastery’s.
Mastery’s calendar marks early dismissals on December 23, February 9, May 7 and June 11 (the last day). Ask Change 4 A Dollar whether it covers those afternoons.
The School District’s list gives Mastery Prep as kindergarten to 3rd grade; Mastery’s own page says kindergarten to 6th grade, which is what this page uses.
If you know a program that serves Mastery Prep and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Girard Academic Music Program
dismissalNote: GAMP’s site doesn’t post its bell schedule; its after-school clubs start at 3:00 pm
notes: GAMP’s own weekly club schedule lists clubs from 3:00 to 4:00 pm: gospel choir on Mondays; arts and crafts, board games and chess on Tuesdays; Dungeons and Dragons, Scrabble (middle school, October to March), dance and others on Wednesdays; and Girls on the Run on Tuesdays and Thursdays, 3:00 to 4:30 pm, March to May. The schedule isn’t dated, so ask which are meeting this year. They have a listing here.

GAMP’s music groups and productions (All City ensembles, musical theatre, swing band for middle school) and its sports teams are on its extracurricular and athletics pages; most of the bands and crews are for high school.
GAMP teaches 5th to 12th grade, so there is nothing here for younger children. We found no daily after-school care on its site; ask the office.
If you know a program that serves GAMP and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Esperanza Academy Charter School: Elementary
aliases: Esperanza Academy Charter School (W Hunting Park Ave)
address: 201 W Hunting Park Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19140
dismissalNote: Esperanza’s site doesn’t post the elementary bell schedule. Its calendar has students leave at 1:00 pm on most Wednesdays (professional learning days)
notes: The City’s program locator lists ASPIRA’s after-school program for Esperanza, the ASPIRA Children’s Achievement Program, for kindergarten to 5th grade: free, Monday to Friday, 2:45 to 6:00 pm, from November 4, 2026 to June 8, 2027, with a hot meal and a snack. The City’s listing gives its address as 301 W Hunting Park Ave, Esperanza’s upper-grades building a block west, so ask ASPIRA where elementary children go and how they get there. It has a listing here.
Esperanza’s own site lists after-school clubs for its elementary students: a robotics club two days a week and a chess club, both led by its teachers. They have a listing here.

Esperanza keeps its own calendar, and its days off aren’t the District’s: it is closed for report card conferences on November 11 (Veterans Day) and April 14, its winter recess runs to January 5 with a professional development day on January 6, and students leave at 1:00 pm on most Wednesdays. The days off on this page come from its calendar; the days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against Esperanza’s. Ask ASPIRA whether its program opens early on the 1:00 pm Wednesdays.
This page is for Esperanza’s elementary school at 201 W Hunting Park Ave. Its middle school is at 4261 N 5th St and its high school at 301 W Hunting Park Ave.
If you know a program that serves Esperanza Elementary and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Horatio B. Hackett School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:45 am to 3:24 pm
notes: Hackett’s own site lists these after-school programs: After-School All-Stars, Cione Recreation Center, First Class Learning Academy, PlayArts, Shissler Recreation Center and STEM Prep Academy.
PlayArts runs its after-school program inside Hackett, from dismissal to 6:00 pm, for Pre-K to 5th grade. It has a listing here.
Shissler Recreation Center picks up Hackett students, according to the City’s program data, and Hackett names it too. It has a listing here.
The others Hackett names are under “Also named on Hackett’s site”: we couldn’t confirm on their own pages or the City’s that they serve Hackett.
Hackett’s own clubs (the Green Team, choir, band, strings, the Page Turners, Movement Makers and more) have a listing here.
If you know a program that serves Hackett and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

notes: Mastery Cleveland’s own page says before care and aftercare at the school are run by Baywaycares, Monday to Friday, from 6:30 am to the start of school and from dismissal to 6:00 pm, and that childcare subsidies are accepted. It has a listing here; the page doesn’t give a price, so ask.

The page also lists the school’s own teams and clubs: basketball, cheerleading, flag football, track and field, soccer, volleyball, a Settlement band, and mentoring, photography and yearbook, hairstyling, book, fashion, fitness and gaming clubs. They have a listing here.

Mastery Cleveland follows the Mastery Schools calendar, not the District’s. Its days off on this page come from Mastery’s 2026–27 Philadelphia calendar: it closes for Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, and its spring break is March 22 to 26. The days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against Mastery’s.
Mastery’s calendar marks early dismissals on December 23, February 9, May 7 and June 11 (the last day). Ask Baywaycares whether it covers those afternoons.
The school takes students who live in its attendance zone in 19140; the page has the map.
If you know a program that serves Mastery Cleveland and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

Northwood keeps its own calendar, not the District’s. notes: Mastery Mann’s own page says before care and aftercare at the school are run by Mastermindz: before care 7:00 to 8:00 am, aftercare from dismissal to 6:00 pm, Monday to Friday, with enrollment and a monthly fee. It has a listing here; the page doesn’t give the fee, so ask the main office.

The page also lists the school’s clubs and activities: academic enrichment, art, Aspiring Divas, basketball, book, dance, flag football, math and step clubs, National Honor Society, school musicals and student leadership. They have a listing here.

Mastery Mann follows the Mastery Schools calendar, not the District’s. Its days off on this page come from Mastery’s 2026–2027 Philadelphia calendar: it closes for Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, and its spring break is March 22 to March 26. The days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against Mastery’s.
Mastery’s calendar marks early dismissals on December 23, February 9, May 7 and June 11 (the last day). Ask Mastermindz whether it covers those afternoons.
The school is in Wynnefield and takes students who live in its attendance zone in 19131; the page has the map. Students can go on to Mastery’s Shoemaker Campus after 6th grade.
If you know a program that serves Mastery Mann and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: James Dobson School
dismissalNote: the school’s site gives the school day as 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, with kindergarten dismissed at 3:30 pm, grades 1–2 at 3:33 pm and grades 3–5 at 3:35 pm
notes: North Light Community Center’s KidZone, on Green Lane, offers before care to Dobson students and after care with transportation from the school. It has a listing here.

Dobson’s site lists after-school enrichment, a LEGO robotics team, a gardening club, Reading Olympics, a cultural arts club and a student leadership group, plus girls’ volleyball and softball, elementary intramurals and middle-grades sports. They are listed here as the school’s clubs and teams, without days or times, so ask the office which meet after dismissal.
Early dismissal days end at 12:30 pm for kindergarten and 12:39 pm for grades 6–8, according to the school’s site. Ask KidZone whether it covers those afternoons.
If you know a program that serves Dobson and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Shawmont School
dismissalNote: the school’s site gives school hours as 7:30 am to 2:09 pm, with dismissal from 2:00 pm
notes: Roxborough Church’s Roxy After-School Program picks children up from Shawmont each day and takes them back to the church on Ridge Avenue. It has a listing here.

Shawmont’s site lists an art club, game club, garden club, stock market club, tutoring, yearbook and a middle school girls group, and sports through Philadelphia Youth Basketball, golf, track and the Middle Grades Conference. It names Action Karate, Big Brothers Big Sisters, Philadelphia Youth Basketball and Enchantment Theatre Company as community partners. They are listed here as the school’s clubs and partners, without days or times, so ask the office which meet after dismissal.
Staff are in the schoolyard from 7:00 am for students who arrive early, according to the school’s site. For early dismissals the site points to its parent and student handbook.
If you know a program that serves Shawmont and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.
alsoListed: North Light Community Center’s KidZone: its registration form lists Shawmont among the schools it transports from, but its own page doesn’t name Shawmont, so ask KidZone.
The Schuylkill Center: a magazine roundup lists van pickup from Shawmont; the Center’s own site couldn’t be read, so ask the Center.

name: A. L. Fitzpatrick School
dismissalNote: the school’s site gives the school day as 7:30 am to 2:09 pm, with pupils dismissed between 1:50 and 2:09 pm
notes: Fitzpatrick’s community partners page names the YMCA for grades K to 4 and the Philadelphia Youth Network (PYN) for grades 5 to 8. The YMCA runs its paid Before & After School Enrichment program at the school for kindergarten to 4th grade, and PYN runs its AIM Afterschool program there for middle schoolers. Both have listings here.

Fitzpatrick’s site lists its 2026–2027 clubs: basketball skills training, yoga, yearbook, crafting, tech, chess, painting techniques, Girls on the Run, gardening, guitar, middle school student council and PBIS, plus soccer and track and field for grades 6 to 8. They are listed here as the school’s clubs, without days or times, so ask the office which meet after dismissal.
Students can enter for breakfast from 7:00 am, according to the school’s site. Its monthly calendars are posted from the calendar page; ask the office about early dismissal days.
If you know a program that serves Fitzpatrick and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Abram S. Jenks School
dismissalNote: the school’s site gives the school day as 8:15 to 2:50, ending at 11:50 am on half days
notes: Beehive @ Bok lists Jenks among the schools it picks up from, Monday to Friday. Its list says only “Jenks”; the other schools on it are all in South Philadelphia, so it is listed here as this Jenks, not J.S. Jenks in Chestnut Hill. Ask Beehive to confirm.

For clubs after school, parents meet students in the schoolyard and sign them out. They are listed here as the school’s clubs.
Half days end at 11:50 am, according to the school’s site. Ask Beehive whether it covers those afternoons.
The school’s site has an after-school section that points to the City’s program locator, and its community partnerships section is empty.
If you know a program that serves A.S. Jenks and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.
